pull.title: test: construct fee estimator test transactions declaratively
pull.body:
Part of #36692. 

`blockpolicyestimator_tests`: Replace the transaction template, whose `prevout` index was overwritten to make each `txid` unique, with `make_tx()`, which constructs each transaction with `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` constructor calls.

Move the code that submits a transaction to the estimator, which was repeated in three places, into `add_tx()`. Each transaction is now built once and shared between its mempool entry and the estimator. The transactions submitted to the estimator and its estimates are unchanged.

`mempool_fee_estimator_tests`: Construct the input and output of `MakeRandomTx()` in place instead of resizing the vectors and assigning each field afterwards. Apart from the random `prevout` hash, the transaction is identical to before.

events.body: Addressed some nits on stale comments([comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36797#discussion_r4516296041) & [comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36797#discussion_r4514583637)) and change the arguments in `add_tx` method [comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36797#discussion_r4516235360).

comments.body: This comment is not accurate anymore.

The extraction hides the `blocknum` dependency that the inline code made visible: `add_tx(j, k)` reads `blocknum`, which changes between calls, through the capture.

I would recommend at least passing the arguments that change between calls:

```cpp
const auto add_tx{[&](CAmount fee, int height, uint32_t prevout_n) {...}
```

A standalone function with no captured state would probably be ideal, but to stay in the scope of #36692 I would stick to that.

Follow-up to the add_tx signature suggestion above:
```cpp
mempool_txs[j].push_back(add_tx(feeV[j], blocknum, 10000 * blocknum + 100 * j + k)); // make transaction unique
```
There’s no local entry anymore, so the second half of this comment is stale.

Personal preference: I really dislike curly braces directly attached to variable names. I think it severely impacts readability. I prefer to always use `=` for initialization, with the type on the right-hand side when explicit construction is required. This provides a clear visual separation between the variable declaration and its initializer.

| Rather than | I prefer |
|---|---|
| `int count{0};` | `auto count = 0;` |
| `std::string name{"foo"};` | `auto name = std::string{"foo"};` |
| `Widget widget{};` | `auto widget = Widget{};` |
| `Widget widget{a, b};` | `auto widget = Widget{a, b};` |
| `std::vector<int> v{1, 2, 3};` | `auto v = std::vector{1, 2, 3};` |
| `auto f{[a](int x) { return x + a; }};` | `auto f = [a](int x) { return x + a; };` |
